title.en: Seven calm letters and three long vowels

words.en: aunt or uncle (father's younger brother or sister)

explanation.short: Thai words are built from consonant letters with vowel signs around them. Here are seven consonants (ก จ ด ต บ ป อ) and three long vowels (า as in "father", ี as in "see", ู as in "moon"): ดี sounds like "dee", ปู like "poo".
explanation.more: These seven consonants are called the "mid class", and the class of the first letter will decide the tone later. Every Thai syllable has a tone (mid, low, falling, high or rising). A syllable that ends in a long vowel, like these, is said in the plain mid tone: level, like your calm speaking voice. Note that ต is a t with no puff of air (between d and t), and ป is a p with no puff (between b and p); the letter อ is a silent holder when it starts a word, so อา is just "aa".

checks.prompt: How is ดี said? (It starts with the d sound.)
How is ปู said? (ป is a p without a puff of air.)
